facts.statement: The genus Calsoyasuchus is known from a single incomplete skull that is unusually derived for an Early Jurassic crocodylomorph.
facts.quote: Formally described as C. valliceps, it is known from a single incomplete skull which is unusually derived for such an early crocodile relative.

facts.statement: Calsoyasuchus was formally described in 2002 by Ronald Tykoski and colleagues.
facts.quote: This genus was described in 2002 by Ronald Tykoski and colleagues

facts.statement: Fossils of Calsoyasuchus were found in the Kayenta Formation on Navajo Nation land in Coconino County, Arizona.
facts.quote: Its fossilized remains were found in the Sinemurian-Pliensbachian-age Kayenta Formation on Navajo Nation land in Coconino County, Arizona, United States.

facts.statement: The preserved skull of Calsoyasuchus is approximately 38.0 centimeters (15.0 inches) long.
facts.quote: As preserved, it is about 38.0 centimeters (15.0 in) long, making its owner a moderately sized animal.

facts.statement: The skull of Calsoyasuchus was long, low, and curved with both ends higher than the middle.
facts.quote: The skull was long, low, and curved so that both extremities were higher than the middle.

facts.statement: The left maxilla of the holotype skull is more complete than the right and contains at least 29 teeth.
facts.quote: The left maxilla (main tooth-bearing bone of the upper jaw) is more complete than the right, and had at least 29 teeth.

facts.statement: A deep groove runs along the midline of the nasal and frontal bones of the skull.
facts.quote: There was a deep groove along the midline of the nasals and the frontals

facts.statement: Unlike derived neosuchians, Calsoyasuchus possessed external antorbital fenestrae.
facts.quote: Unlike derived neosuchians, it had external antorbital fenestrae.

facts.statement: CT scanning revealed that Calsoyasuchus had a double-walled secondary palate similar to true crocodylians and pneumatic cavities.
facts.quote: Tykoski and colleagues subjected the skull to CT scanning, which revealed internal cavities and air passages, and showed that it had a double-walled secondary palate similar to that of true crocodylians, and similar pneumatic cavities as well.

facts.statement: Calsoyasuchus was a crocodylomorph that lived during the Early Jurassic period.
facts.quote: Calsoyasuchus (meaning "[Dr. Kyril] Calsoyas' crocodile") is a genus of crocodylomorph that lived in the Early Jurassic.

facts.statement: Calsoyasuchus lived between 199.5 and 184.2 million years ago during the Sinemurian and Pliensbachian ages.
facts.quote: Time range: Sinemurian to Pliensbachian (199.5 to 184.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: A 2022 analysis suggested Calsoyasuchus is the sister group of Thalattosuchia.
facts.quote: A 2022 analysis found it to be the sister group of Thalattosuchia.

facts.statement: The Kayenta Formation during the Early Jurassic contained a diverse fauna including caecilians, frogs, turtles, multiple crocodylomorphs, pterosaurs, dinosaurs, and early mammal relatives.
facts.quote: During the Sinemurian and Pliensbachian ages of the Early Jurassic, the Kayenta Formation had a diverse fauna, with the remains of caecilians, frogs, turtles, at least five other taxa of crocodylomorphs, pterosaurs, theropod, sauropodomorph, and ornithischian dinosaurs, and early relatives of mammals (tritylodontids and morganucodontids).
